battery.name: Vehicle Battery
battery.function: Supplies electrical energy to start the engine and power electronic accessories when the engine is off.
battery.working: Chemical reactions between lead plates and sulfuric acid electrolyte produce direct current (DC) electricity, typically at 12 volts.
common_problems: Dead cell or sulfation resulting in failure to hold charge
Terminal corrosion causing high resistance and starting failure
Alternator or stator charging system failure draining the battery
Parasitic draw draining battery overnight
maintenance: Clean terminal posts with wire brush and baking soda solution
Check resting terminal voltage (healthy is 12.6V or above)
Ensure electrolyte level is adequate in flooded lead-acid batteries
Verify charging voltage while engine runs (13.8V to 14.4V)

spark_plug.name: Spark Plug
spark_plug.function: Delivers an electric spark to ignite the compressed air-fuel mixture in the cylinder combustion chamber.
spark_plug.working: High-voltage electricity from the ignition coil arcs across the center and ground electrode gap at precisely timed intervals.
common_problems: Carbon fouling from rich fuel mixture or incomplete combustion
Electrode gap erosion causing misfires and weak spark
Oil contamination from leaking valve stem seals or piston rings
Engine hesitation, rough idling, and poor fuel economy
maintenance: Inspect electrode color (light tan/gray indicates healthy combustion)
Measure and set spark plug gap with a feeler gauge to manufacturer spec
Torque to proper specification to avoid cylinder head thread damage
Replace every 15,000 to 30,000 km for standard copper or 80,000 km for iridium

brake_rotor.name: Brake Rotor (Disc)
brake_rotor.function: Provides a flat, rotating friction surface that brake pads clamp onto to decelerate or stop the vehicle.
brake_rotor.working: The hydraulic brake caliper squeezes brake pads against both faces of the spinning rotor, converting kinetic energy into heat.
common_problems: Rotor warping caused by excessive thermal stress, leading to pulsating brake pedal or lever
Deep grooves and scoring from worn-out brake pad backplates
Excessive thinning below minimum manufacturer stamp thickness
Surface rust or glaze reducing friction coefficient
maintenance: Measure disc thickness with a micrometer or vernier caliper
Inspect rotor face visually for heat discoloration, deep cracks, and grooves
Clean brake dust using designated brake cleaner spray
Never spray lubricants or degreasers near rotor surface

brake_pad.name: Brake Pads
brake_pad.function: High-friction material that contacts the brake rotor to generate braking torque.
brake_pad.working: Pushed directly by hydraulic caliper pistons when brake lever or pedal is pressed.
common_problems: Excessive friction material wear down to metal backing plate
Squealing noise caused by acoustic wear indicators contacting the disc
Uneven pad wear due to seized caliper slide pins
Glazing from prolonged high-temperature riding or driving
maintenance: Inspect pad thickness regularly (replace if lining is below 2-3 mm)
Ensure caliper slide pins are cleaned and lubricated with silicone grease
Bed in new brake pads properly with gradual braking cycles

brake_caliper.name: Brake Caliper
brake_caliper.function: Houses the brake pistons and holds the brake pads in proper alignment over the rotor.
brake_caliper.working: Hydraulic brake fluid pressure pushes the internal piston(s) outward to clamp the pads onto the rotor.
common_problems: Piston seizure due to moisture, corrosion, or old brake fluid
Fluid leaks past rubber piston dust seals
Stuck slider pins causing dragging brakes and overheating
Spongy brake lever/pedal from air bubbles trapped in caliper lines
maintenance: Flush and bleed brake fluid every 1 to 2 years (DOT 4 or DOT 5.1)
Inspect rubber boots and seals for splits or fluid leakage
Clean caliper assembly of brake dust and road grime

radiator.name: Radiator
radiator.function: Dissipates excess engine heat by transferring heat from engine coolant to the ambient air stream.
radiator.working: Hot coolant flows through narrow aluminum tubes with thin cooling fins while air passes through, cooling the liquid.
common_problems: Coolant leaks from cracked plastic tanks or corroded tube seams
Bent or obstructed cooling fins blocking airflow
Internal sludge or scale clogging coolant circulation
Overheating engine and boiling coolant overflow
maintenance: Straighten bent radiator cooling fins with a fin comb
Flush and refill cooling system with 50/50 ethylene glycol coolant mix
Inspect radiator cap pressure seal for rubber degradation
Rinse away bugs, dirt, and mud using low-pressure water spray

headlights.name: Headlight Assembly
headlights.function: Illuminates the roadway ahead for nighttime operation and enhances vehicle visibility to other motorists.
headlights.working: Uses halogen filament, HID xenon arc, or LED diodes focused through a parabolic reflector and polycarbonate lens.
common_problems: Burnt-out halogen bulb filaments or failed LED driver ballast
Cloudy, yellowed, or oxidized polycarbonate lens blocking light output
Moisture condensation inside sealed housing from degraded gasket
Misfocused or misaligned beam angle blinding oncoming traffic
maintenance: Restore oxidized lenses with headlight polishing and UV sealant
Check beam vertical and horizontal alignment on a flat wall at 25 feet
Never touch halogen bulb glass with bare fingers (oils cause early failure)
Inspect wiring harness connectors for melting or loose ground pins

rim.name: Wheel Rim
rim.function: Supports the tire bead, carries vehicle load, and transmits drive and braking forces.
rim.working: Bolts directly to wheel hub; maintains airtight seal with tubeless tire bead.
common_problems: Bent or cracked rim lip from striking severe potholes or curbs
Slow bead air leak due to corrosion or rim edge deformation
Wheel unbalance causing high-speed steering wobble
Stress fractures around lug nut holes or spokes
maintenance: Perform periodic dynamic wheel balancing and tire rotation
Torque wheel lug nuts or axle nuts with a calibrated torque wrench
Inspect inner and outer rim lips for dents, cracks, or paint peeling

oil_filter.name: Engine Oil Filter
oil_filter.function: Traps abrasive metal particulates, carbon soot, and debris from engine oil before recirculation.
oil_filter.working: Pressurized oil is forced through porous synthetic or cellulose pleats inside a steel canister or cartridge.
common_problems: Clogged filter media opening the internal bypass valve (allowing dirty oil)
Rubber O-ring gasket leak causing low oil pressure and oil loss
Over-tightened canister crushing the gasket or stripping threads
Collapsed filter element from excessive oil viscosity or cold starts
maintenance: Replace oil filter at every scheduled engine oil change
Lubricate the rubber O-ring gasket with clean motor oil before spinning on
Hand-tighten plus 3/4 turn (avoid over-torquing with filter wrench)

starter.name: Starter Motor
starter.function: Spins the engine flywheel or crankshaft to initiate internal combustion.
starter.working: An integrated electromagnetic solenoid pushes a bendix pinion gear into mesh with the flywheel ring gear while switching high current to the DC motor.
common_problems: Worn starter carbon brushes causing intermittent or no-crank condition
Solenoid click without motor spinning due to burnt internal contacts
Worn bendix gear teeth grinding against the flywheel ring gear
Slow cranking under load due to weak starter or corroded battery cable
maintenance: Verify battery health and clean main ground and positive terminal cables
Listen for single click (solenoid good, motor/battery weak) vs rapid clicking
Avoid cranking continuously for more than 10 seconds to prevent overheating

piston.name: Engine Piston
piston.function: Transfers force from combustion gas expansion to the crankshaft via the connecting rod.
piston.working: Moves reciprocally inside cylinder bore, compressing fuel mixture and receiving combustion force.
common_problems: Piston ring wear causing blow-by gas, high crankcase pressure, and blue exhaust smoke
Piston skirt scuffing from oil starvation or engine overheating
Piston crown detonation damage from low-octane fuel or improper ignition timing
Low cylinder compression resulting in hard starting and loss of power
maintenance: Use specified engine oil grade and change at scheduled intervals
Prevent engine overheating by maintaining radiator/cooling fins
Perform periodic cylinder compression test (benchmark 120-170 PSI)

cylinder_head.name: Cylinder Head
cylinder_head.function: Houses intake/exhaust valves, spark plugs, and camshaft(s), sealing the top of combustion chambers.
cylinder_head.working: Fastened tightly to engine block with head bolts, sealing combustion pressures and coolant/oil passages through a multi-layer steel head gasket.
common_problems: Blown cylinder head gasket allowing coolant into combustion chamber or oil sump
Warped mating surface from severe engine overheating
Hairline cracks between valve seats causing combustion leaks
Worn valve guides or stem seals causing oil burning
maintenance: Never continue running an overheated engine
Verify head bolt torque sequence and values when servicing
Check for milky oil on oil cap (sign of coolant mixing into oil)

clutch_plate.name: Clutch Friction Plate / Assembly
clutch_plate.function: Connects and disconnects engine power from transmission gearbox for shifting and starting.
clutch_plate.working: Friction material plates pressed against steel pressure plates transmit torque via spring pressure until disengaged by clutch lever or pedal.
common_problems: Clutch slippage under acceleration (engine revs rise without speed increase)
Burnt friction lining from riding the clutch or aggressive starts
Clutch dragging or hard gear shifts due to improper cable free-play
Warped steel plates causing clutch judder or shuddering when taking off
maintenance: Maintain proper clutch cable free play (10-15 mm at lever tip for bikes)
In wet clutch motorcycles, strictly use JASO MA/MA2 motorcycle oils (no friction modifiers)
Avoid riding or holding the clutch at red lights

alternator.name: Alternator / Stator Magneto
alternator.function: Generates alternating current (AC) electricity while the engine runs to power systems and recharge the battery.
alternator.working: Rotor electromagnet spins inside stationary stator coils; internal diodes rectify AC to DC voltage controlled by an internal regulator.
common_problems: Worn rotor brushes or failed voltage regulator overcharging or undercharging
Blown rectifier diode allowing battery discharge or AC ripple noise
Noisy or seized alternator pulley bearings causing belt squeal
Battery warning light illuminating on dashboard instrument cluster
maintenance: Check charging voltage across battery terminals while running (13.8V - 14.4V)
Inspect serpentine or drive belt tension and rib condition
Ensure alternator cooling vents are clear of grease and oil leaks

transmission.name: Transmission Gearbox
transmission.function: Alters gear ratios between engine crankshaft and drive wheels to optimize torque and speed.
transmission.working: Pairs input shaft gears with output shaft countershaft gears, shifted via selector forks and dog clutches or synchromesh sleeves.
common_problems: Grinding noise during gear engagement due to worn synchronizer rings
Gears popping out of mesh under acceleration due to worn dogs or detents
Whining bearing noise originating from transmission input shaft
Low gear oil causing extreme friction, gear tooth chipping, and overheating
maintenance: Inspect transmission gear oil level and replace at recommended service intervals
Always fully depress clutch before selecting gears to avoid dog tooth rounding
Inspect output shaft seal for oil seepage around drive sprocket or CV joint

fuel_injector.name: Electronic Fuel Injector
fuel_injector.function: Sprays finely atomized fuel into the intake port or combustion chamber under precise ECU command.
fuel_injector.working: An internal solenoid or piezo actuator lifts a micro-pintle valve, allowing high-pressure fuel to atomize through precision micro-orifices.
common_problems: Clogged nozzle orifices from gum and fuel lacquer deposits
Leaking injector pintle causing flooded cylinders, rich mixture, and black smoke
Sticking solenoid causing random engine misfires and rough idle
Degraded rubber O-rings causing external fuel or vacuum leaks
maintenance: Use quality fuel with detergents and change fuel filter regularly
Run professional ultrasonic injector cleaning or fuel system additives
Replace upper and lower Viton O-rings whenever injectors are removed
